body:
Global crypto markets ended Thursday in a subdued holding pattern, with total market capitalization sitting at $2.28T after a -0.36% decline over the past 24 hours. 24-hour volume came in at $65.7B, a figure that signals neither conviction selling nor meaningful accumulation. BTC dominance held at 56.6% and ETH dominance at 10.1%, and the Fear & Greed index printed 28 today versus 29 yesterday, a whisker deeper into Fear territory and consistent with a market that is digesting rather than directing. The mood is best described as cautious consolidation: no panic, but no appetite either. Microsoft's AI-driven equity rally provided a mild halo effect per CoinDesk's live coverage, enough to keep spot bids present but not enough to generate any real follow-through momentum in digital assets.

BTC is trading at $64,409, down -0.40% over 24 hours and off -1.80% on the week, though the 1-hour print of +0.50% suggests short-term buyers have stepped in around this zone. The $64,000 handle is the line in the sand right now — clean psychological support, and the fact that BTC is holding near it rather than through it means the level is being tested rather than defended with conviction. A CoinDesk headline flagged $286 million in leveraged bet liquidations from recent BTC and ETH whipsaw action, which explains some of the volatility without a clean directional resolution. Analysts cited in CoinDesk's Fed coverage agree the Federal Reserve's hold was hawkish in tone but remain split on implications for BTC price action from here. Watch $64,000 as support and any reclaim of $65,000+ as the earliest signal that short-term sellers have exhausted themselves.

ETH is at $1,916.42, down -0.40% over 24 hours and essentially flat on the week at -0.10%, making it one of the more resilient assets in the tracked universe on a 7-day basis. Volume was $9.85B, healthy relative to its market position. The divergence story today belongs to UNI, which is the clear standout across the ZIMR tracked universe with a +5.40% 24-hour gain to $4.02 and a +5.20% 7-day move — no obvious single-catalyst explanation available in the data, but the volume of $0.28B warrants attention. BNB also bucked the trend, printing +1.30% on the day to $577.6 and extending a +1.50% weekly gain, suggesting Binance-ecosystem positioning is quietly firming. On the weak side, XRP dropped -1.00% to $1.08 and is down -4.90% on the week, SOL fell -0.60% to $73.94 with a painful -4.40% weekly print, ADA is at $0.164685 and bleeding -5.10% on the week, and DOT at $0.767764 is the worst weekly performer in the tracked group at -6.30%. The pattern is clear: layer-1 alternatives are underperforming while DEX-adjacent and exchange-native tokens find marginal bids.

The macro backdrop is doing the heavy lifting in terms of explaining direction and mood. The Fed's hold was read as hawkish, per multiple analyst sources, and that removes a near-term catalyst for risk assets broadly. US sanctions on an Iranian maritime firm that reportedly accepted Bitcoin to evade restrictions, per Cointelegraph, adds a regulatory friction narrative that institutional desks will note. South Korea's proposal to implement stablecoin rules ahead of broader crypto legislation signals that regulatory scaffolding is being erected globally in a piecemeal fashion. On the ETF front, CoinTelegraph reports Bitcoin ETF inflows have returned while Ether funds slipped into outflows — a bifurcation that reinforces BTC's dominant positioning but raises questions about institutional appetite for ETH at current levels. Australia suing Telegram over alleged failures to remove terror content is a reminder that the regulatory perimeter around adjacent infrastructure is tightening.

Looking ahead, the key watch points are BTC's ability to hold $64,000 into the weekend and whether ETF inflow momentum for BTC can build into next week's trading. A confirmed break below $64,000 on volume would bring the $62,000 area into focus and likely accelerate the alt-coin bleed already visible in SOL, ADA, and DOT. On the upside, any dovish pivot signal from Fed speakers or a meaningful equity risk-on session could be the trigger for a short-squeeze attempt given the recent liquidation activity. The UNI spike deserves monitoring — either it fades quickly and confirms a low-liquidity pump, or it attracts follow-on momentum that signals broader DeFi rotation. Regulatory developments around stablecoins in South Korea and any further US enforcement actions using Bitcoin transaction data are the macro-regulatory wildcards for the week ahead. The picture changes bullishly on a sustained hold above $65,000 BTC with renewed ETF inflows across both BTC and ETH; it changes bearishly if Fear & Greed slips further and spot volume fails to recover above current levels.
